backtest.note: Two modes, both labelled. The in-sample and forward numbers are CONTAMINATED: their features are season-to-date leaderboards that contain the games being graded. mode_meaning.contaminated: Team inputs are season-to-date leaderboards, so every graded game sits inside its own features. This measures calibration, not skill, and it cannot validate anything.
mode_meaning.vintage: Every game is priced on a leaderboard snapshot whose knowledge cutoff is strictly before that game: team offense, team run prevention, the starter's SEM+ ratings and the park index all come out of that snapshot. WHICH starter does not: his identity is the probable on the completed-game row, which is the final feed's, while the served board prices the probable listed at the nightly build. Who starts is fixed before first pitch, so that is a difference in information and not an outcome leak. A game with no such snapshot is skipped, not graded on today's numbers, and a game whose snapshot predates the stored park column is priced with the park term at neutral rather than on the live index. This is the only mode that can validate the model.

method.pitchers: rest-of-season rate per inning from the projection engine, times the pitcher's measured innings per start
method.hitters: rest-of-season rate per plate appearance times expected PA for the projected lineup slot, counted by slot on the 2022-2024 play-by-play corpus and split home from away, because the home club does not bat in the ninth when it leads. Run environment and extra innings are not conditioned on: neither is knowable before the game
method.slot_pa_basis: starter plate appearances by lineup slot, counted on the cached play-by-play corpus over the 2022-2024 seasons (131,202 starter-games), split home from away, and checked once against a 2025 hold-out; each side's nine slots sum under that side's own PA per team-game (away 37.07 of 38.46, home 35.47 of 36.81). Where a row fell back instead, the row says so in expected_pa_basis
method.lineup_assumption: projected order against the opposing probable's throwing hand: the vs-LHP order when the probable throws left, the vs-RHP order otherwise, resolved for the whole slate in one bulk StatsAPI call. An unknown hand falls back to the vs-RHP order and each hitter row says so in vs_hand_basis. Posted lineup cards are not read
method.distribution: declared per prop market; every row carries the one that priced it, and the value block prices the same function at the book's line. No props row has settled, so no choice is calibrated against outcomes

distribution_by_market.rule: each prop market declares one distribution, and the row carries which one priced it in `pmf`. The value block prices the SAME function at the book's line, so the two tables cannot disagree about one bet

Strikeouts.reason: a batter faced is struck out or is not, so the count is a sum of Bernoulli trials with support capped at batters faced, and Poisson puts mass on more strikeouts than batters, which cannot happen. On the served 5.5 line the binomial also prices better than Poisson, by a paired Brier of 0.001045 with an interval excluding zero. It does NOT fit the shape better: the real count over-disperses against the binomial by 1.400x and against Poisson by only 1.095x. Measured in data/betting_props_dark_eval.json

Hits allowed.reason: one batter faced yields at most one hit, the same Bernoulli argument as strikeouts

Earned runs.reason: earned runs are not a per-batter indicator: one plate appearance can score four. The count is a compound sum with no per-trial cap, so the binomial argument does not apply and Poisson is the stated approximation. It understates the tail of a clumped scoring distribution

Total bases.reason: total bases per plate appearance take values 0 to 4, so the count is a compound sum, not a sum of indicators. A binomial would be wrong in the other direction, and the extra-base mix a compound distribution needs is not carried on the row. Poisson stays, now stated rather than assumed

1+ hits.reason: a plate appearance yields at most one hit, so hits over a game are binomial over plate appearances. This is the market the two surfaces disagreed on: the fair line already used the Bernoulli reading and the value block used Poisson

1+ home runs.reason: at most one home run per plate appearance, the same Bernoulli argument as hits

Outs recorded.reason: published as a fair number only; no over line is priced, so no mass function is claimed for it

distribution_by_market.not_claimed: no props row has ever settled, so none of these distributions is calibrated against outcomes. The choice is structural, not measured

method.market_view: the team board's _market_view verbatim: consensus line by book count, prices shopped on that line only, fair probabilities from the minimum-hold book, staleness / hold / consensus-distance rejections counted per pair
method.model_prob: the props fair-line lambda (vs-hand order, A5a) evaluated at the BOOK's consensus line through the SAME mass function the fair-line table publishes (_props_side_probabilities, distribution declared per market in PROPS_DISTRIBUTIONS), push-conditioned on whole numbers. rules.when: two or more legs from the same game
rules.why: Same-game outcomes share the run environment, the starters and the weather. Multiplying the legs assumes an independence they do not have.

rules.when: moneyline and runline on the same team
rules.why: The runline is a subset of the moneyline: one bet with two prices. The product is meaningless.

rules.when: a moneyline and the total in the same game
rules.why: Favourite plus under and dog plus over are both positively correlated. The naive product is too cheap.

rules.when: two player props from the same lineup
rules.why: Teammates share innings and baserunners. Hits and total bases on the same night rise and fall together.

rules.when: a starter strikeout prop with that team's moneyline
rules.why: A dominant start moves both. Correlated legs price differently than the product suggests.

parlay_context.featured_reason: No parlay has a backtest that survives the correlation haircut.
parlay_context.math_note: Independent legs multiply. Same-game legs do not: on positively correlated legs the naive product understates the parlay's probability, at a price no book will sell.

record_label: Provisional. This selection clears a 6.0% floor that was chosen as policy, not measured. The model is unvalidated: 722 of the 600 games the honest backtest needs are graded, and no minimum-edge threshold exists. Recorded before the result.

dugout_context.head: Dugout context, not priced
dugout_context.not_priced_sentence: Dugout context sits beside the price and enters none of it. No probability, edge, expected value, Kelly figure, slot, badge or record row on this page reads anything from In-Game Management, and no In-Game Management figure is a pricer input.
dugout_context.source_label: Source: In-Game Management, club-season 2026 through 2026-09-24, corpus built 2026-09-25T10:06:36+00:00, read from data/management_board.json.
dugout_context.style_sentence: Style, not skill: each is a signed z-score across the thirty club-seasons of its season, sign as measured. Not an index, no ladder, no plus sign; a frequency has no good direction, and these repeat because they are policy.

style_columns.label: Hook z
style_columns.basis: starter pitch count at removal; a negative z is an earlier hook

style_columns.label: Bench z
style_columns.basis: pinch hitters plus pinch runners per game

dugout_context.shape_dark_sentence: Entries by leverage at entry and inherited runners scored live in the per-club decision ledger files, which this page never reads; the club page draws them.
dugout_context.realized_head: Realized value this season, per family, never summed
dugout_context.realized_sentence: Realized value, not skill. Each figure is the win probability that actually moved after the decision, credited to the club that made it, from the decision to the last play it governed. What the alternative would have produced, the reliever not used, the batter not lifted, the pitch not thrown, is not observed, so this is a record of what happened after a manager acted and not a measure of how well he chose. A reliever who pitched well after a poor choice and a hitter who homered after a bad matchup are both in these numbers.
dugout_context.agent_sentence: The agent is the club-season until the manager ledger lands; a club that changed managers during a season is one row here and two in reality.
dugout_context.overlap_note: No cross-family total exists on any row. The family windows overlap: a club's intentional-walk window sits inside its own reliever's stint window, a pinch-hit plate appearance can contain that club's bunt or steal, and a pinch-run window overlaps the pinch hit before it, so one composite per club-season would double count. Per-family sums only.

units.mwpa: wins, realized value, not skill (wp percentage points divided by 100; the steal's is the house win expectancy change of the steal itself)
units.z: signed style z-score, not an index, not skill
